title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang urges U.S.-China dialogue on 'potentially dangerous' AI
source_used: Stocktwits via Yahoo Finance and BigGo Finance (both relay CNBC)
key_facts: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said late Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 at an event in London that the US "absolutely must" work with Chinese AI companies.
He called the technology "powerful and potentially dangerous" and said dialogue should be enhanced; he told CNBC he maintains dialogues with many researchers in China.
He said the US wants to compete for the world while China wants to protect its own market for local chipmakers, and "somewhere that gets resolved".
He urged the UK to do the same, citing its "intellectual capital" as a possible convener.
The remarks followed Nvidia's announcement of $250 million over five years for AI safety and security research in the UK.
In a separate Bloomberg interview he called AI IPO and data-centre delays "growing pains" and said AI should be treated as critical infrastructure like electricity or water.
Huang has argued against overly restrictive AI rules, unlike OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei who have urged stronger regulation.
quote_evidence: "We absolutely must work with each other, and the reason for that is because we think that this technology is going to be powerful and potentially dangerous," Huang stated, speaking at an event in London.
He reiterated that stance Wednesday, saying AI should be treated as critical infrastructure, akin to electricity or water.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading chip executive publicly backs US-China AI dialogue on safety.
